narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and based on an automated assessment of your financial profile, the system determined that you represent too high a credit risk at this time, resulting in a denial of your request. The model estimated a 59% probability that you would struggle to repay the loan — a figure that, while not overwhelmingly high, was sufficient to tip the decision toward denial.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the length of the loan you requested: 48 months, which is more than double the average of roughly 19 months seen among applicants who were approved. A longer repayment period means more time during which financial circumstances can change, and lenders view extended commitments as carrying substantially more risk. This duration, more than anything else in your profile, drove the system's concern about your application.

The second major factor was the status of your checking account, which currently shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about one in five had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no checking account or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals that your current financial situation may already be under strain, making it harder to take on additional debt obligations.

On a more positive note, the amount you requested — 4,308 DM — actually worked slightly in your favor relative to the other factors. While it is higher than the average of around 2,887 DM among approved applicants, the system did not weigh this as heavily against you as the duration and account status, and it contributed a small push in the direction of a favorable assessment.

Other aspects of your profile, such as your employment duration of less than one year and your current rental housing situation, are less common among approved applicants and may have added background pressure to the decision, even if they were not among the top drivers. To improve your chances in a future application, you might consider requesting a shorter loan term, working to bring your checking account into a positive balance, and waiting until you have accumulated more employment stability. Reapplying after addressing these areas could meaningfully shift the outcome in your favor.
